atoms.b:
Early civilizations and first colonies
American history began long before European settlement. ((Native_Americans)) first populated the North American continent around 15,000 BC. ((Christopher_Columbus)), the man often credited with “discovering” America, only arrived at its coast in 1492, marking the beginning of centuries of ((colonization)).

The first ((permanent)) English colony in America was ((founded)) in 1607, namely Jamestown, Virginia. Some years later in 1620, a group of English Puritans embarked on their ((journey)) to America on their ship, the Mayflower. Also known as the ((Pilgrim_fathers)), they founded the Plymouth Colony in Massachusetts the same year.

atoms.b:
Native American history
It is important to understand that Native Americans are not one single group. Hundreds of different tribes are recognised by the US ((government)) today, and there used to be many more in the past. Navajo, Cherokee, Apache and Blackfoot are only a few of the most well-known ((tribes)). All have their own culture and history. However, they do share a common history as ((victims)) of colonization.

Although it is difficult to ((estimate)) how many Natives lived in North America pre-colonization, it is clear the indigenous population declined drastically with the arrival of Europeans. For one, they brought with them many diseases that were ((widespread)) in Europe, Africa and Asia, but that Native Americans had not developed an ((immunity)) to. Epidemics of smallpox, influenza and other diseases killed millions of indigenous people.

atoms.b: While some tribes responded ((violently)) to settlers invading their territory, others maintained friendly relations with them, engaging in ((trade)) or forming alliances against enemy tribes. In the end, however, the colonists continued ((claiming)) more land for themselves and forcibly ((driving)) the Natives out of their homes.
